chase_cards.name: No.1 Trainer
chase_cards.why: This is a chase because it is not merely another No.1 Trainer trophy. It is the Best in Japan champion lane: a finals route where the winner's body enters the card image itself, making identity, event, and artifact harder to separate.

key_artists.name: winner photograph / unpromoted production design
examples: No.1 Trainer [Battle Road Summer 2002 Best in Japan]
key_artists.why: The load-bearing visual fact is not a named illustrator credit but the use of the winning player photograph in the card image. That makes the card a personal artifact and an identification trap: an agent should compare photo-card construction and event route, not invent a named illustrator where the attached sources do not supply one.

claims.text: The local catalog models Battle Road Summer 2002 Best in Japan first place prize as one unnumbered promotional source row containing No.1 Trainer at source index 253.
Bulbapedia says the 2002 No.1 Trainer Battle Road Summer print was awarded to winners of the Battle Road Summer 2002 Best in Japan deciding tournament.
Bulbapedia's Elite Four Trainer page places the Battle Road Summer 2002 finals in Tokyo on August 17, after regional events between July 20 and August 11.
Bulbapedia says the 2002 Battle Road Summer Best in Japan No.1 Trainer illustration features a photograph of the card's recipient superimposed on the Battle Road Summer 2002 competition logo.
Bulbapedia gives the 2002 Best in Japan No.1 Trainer text as recognizing that the recipient is the number one trainer in the Pokémon Card Game Official Tournament Battle Road Summer 2002.
Bulbapedia says the Battle Road 2002 series introduced the Master age division for players 18 and over, in addition to Junior and Senior divisions.
Bulbapedia says Battle Road Summer 2002, unlike Spring, culminated in a Best in Japan final with a new card awarded to top ranking players.

Pokumon says Junior league winners of Battle Road Summer 2002 were invited to the International Tropical Mega Battle 2002 in Hawaii, giving the Summer apparatus an international edge beyond the regional and national trophies.

No named illustrator or designer is promoted for this exact row from the attached sources; the visual-credit note is therefore kept as winner-photograph / unpromoted production design rather than an artist attribution.

As judged collector texture, this No.1 Trainer matters because it turns victory into a personal image-object: the route, rank, logo, and winner photograph all have to line up before an agent treats a listing as the Best in Japan first-place card.

Agents should preserve No.1 rank, Battle Road Summer 2002 Best in Japan finals route, source index 253, August 17 Tokyo finals context, winner-photograph construction, Battle Road Summer 2002 logo, and non-equivalence with regional No.1/No.2/No.3 Trainer, Best in Japan No.2/No.3, Elite Four Trainer, Worlds, Neo Road, or generic No.1 Trainer listings before accepting a match.

narrative.human_title: Battle Road Summer 2002 Best in Japan No.1 Trainer: when the winner enters the card
narrative.why_it_matters: The regional trophy cards remember a rank. This card goes further: the winner's photograph becomes part of the object. That changes the whole feeling of the artifact. It is less like a universal badge and more like a small official portrait of a Pokémon moment, a card that says this person, at this final, inside this apparatus, stood at the top. For an agent, the lesson is blunt: do not buy the phrase No.1 Trainer. Follow the route until the photograph, logo, rank, and event all touch.
not_claiming: primary-source exact artist or designer proof

special_identification_instructions.trigger: A listing, want, scan, seller story, slab label, or agent memory says No.1 Trainer, Ｎｏ.１トレーナー, Battle Road Summer 2002, Best in Japan, finals, Tokyo, August 17 2002, winner photograph, competition logo, regional No.1 Trainer, No.2 Trainer, No.3 Trainer, Elite Four Trainer, World Championships, Neo Road, Tropical Mega Battle, or Secret Super Battle.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Identify this row by No.1 Trainer rank plus Battle Road Summer 2002 Best in Japan finals route and winner-photograph card construction, not by famous trophy wording alone.
steps: Confirm the rank is No.1 Trainer / number one trainer, not No.2, No.3, or Elite Four Trainer.
Confirm the route is Battle Road Summer 2002 Best in Japan first place prize, source index 253, not a regional first-place prize.
Look for the finals context: Tokyo final on August 17, 2002 after the July-August regional circuit.
Check whether the card construction includes a winner photograph superimposed on the Battle Road Summer 2002 competition logo; this is a core identity clue, not merely decoration.

Separate this row from Battle Road Summer 2002 regional No.1 Trainer, Spring 2002 regional trophies, Best in Japan No.2/No.3, Elite Four Trainer top-four prize, Worlds No.1 Trainer, Neo Road trophy cards, Tropical Mega Battle, Secret Super Battle, Lizardon Mega Battle, and Kamex Mega Battle.
Do not promote a named illustrator unless a stronger row-level source appears; record the art lane as winner photograph / unpromoted production design.
If a seller offers winner identity, photograph, certificate, tournament paperwork, slab label, or provenance story, treat it as evidence to inspect and hash, not automatic authenticity.

Before any trade gate or spendability decision, require seller-controlled front/back images plus close-ups of title/rank, event text, photograph/logo area, surface/corners, and slab/cert/provenance evidence if claimed.
